THE WORD IS «ZIO», NOT «VICINO», AND THIS ARCHIVE READ IT WRONG. Re-read 16 Sep 2026 at full magnification: the word before «del defunto» is three letters, written twice, and it is not the six-letter «vicino» the same clerk writes on the 1823 and 1825 acts of this same household — those two acts are the control, and they are in this file to be checked against. So the register states in 1824 that the dead child's mother MARIA FALCO is kin to these two men, four years before the 1828 act on which this archive had rested that conclusion. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE. Read strictly, «zio del defunto» makes Maria Falco a SISTER of Pasquale (bapt. 24 October 1767) and of Giuseppe — and therefore a daughter of MATTEO FALCO and FRANCESCA CRISCI. Her own stated age forbids it: twenty-five in June 1824, born about 1799, when Francesca Crisci was bearing children by 1767. Either that age is one of this register's inventions — and this archive holds the same clerk making Giuseppe Falco forty and forty-five four days apart — or «zio» is doing the loose collateral work that «parente» does in 1828. THE WORD IS RECORDED AND THE PEDIGREE IS REFUSED. THE ONLY RECORD IN WHICH PASQUALE FALCO ACTS FOR HIMSELF, and the only document in this archive written in his own hand: the act closes «segnato da noi e da uno de' dichiaranti, avendo l'altro cioè GIUSEPPE FALCO dichiarato di non sapere scrivere per non averlo mai imparato», and beneath it, in a slow upright hand quite unlike the clerk's, stands the signature «PASCALE FALCO» — the Neapolitan form, without the qu, the way he said his own name. His brother could not sign. He is fifty-five here, one year out against his baptism of 24 October 1767 — ordinary — and his trade is COLONO, a tenant farmer, where his death act of 1834 calls him contadino.

The parish entry gave only «Dec 1819» and «nominatus est Aloysius»; this gives the day, the hour, the street and both parents' ages. **ACT NUMBER CORRECTED 20 Sep 2026, from 133 to 134.** The leaf reference was right and the number was not: image 71 left is headed «*Numero d'ordine **CENTOTRENTAQUATTRO***». **Act 133 is on the facing leaf, image 70 right, and it is a different family — «*è comparso **VINCENZO MAURO**, di anni ventisette, di professione viaticale, domiciliato in questo comune strada Sant'Andrea … da **ANDREANA CARFORA** sua moglie legittima, d'anni ventisei, un Maschio***». **Same day, same clerk, a Vincenzo and an Andreana in each** — which is exactly the kind of neighbour an archive chasing act 133 would have taken for its own.

«di anni VENTISEI» — twenty-six. He was given as TWENTY-SEVEN on 10 May 1818, nineteen months earlier: HE GETS YOUNGER BY A YEAR WHILE NINETEEN MONTHS PASS. His baptism of 1 February 1792 makes him twenty-seven here, so both civil figures are wrong and the register is the reason the archive dates him from the font instead.

«d'Anni VENTIDUE» — twenty-two, so b. c.1797. This is the Andreana Crisci who married Vincenzo Falco in December 1814, on his own street and in his own house; she is not the other Andreana Crisci this archive keeps separate.

«*MARITO DI **CAROLINA CIMMINO***» — Luigi Falco's widow, and a person this archive did not know existed. Nothing else about her is established: no marriage act, no parents, no age. **The Arienzo civil marriage record is complete 1809–1858 and holds no Falco–Cimmino wedding**, so they married after 1858 or not at Arienzo.

GENERATION THREE, ALIVE AT SEVENTY-TWO — twenty years later than any sighting this archive had. «*figlio di **VINCENZO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato **alla Camellara***», with **no «fu» and no «defunto»**. **THE FORM MARKS THE DEAD AND THIS REGISTER USES IT**: on the same opening, act 41 gives «*figlio di **fu** Nicola … e della **fu** Colomba Capezzo*», act 43 «*figlia del **fu** Giuseppe … e della **fu** Cecilia Silvestri*», act 45 «*figlia del **fu** Don Stefano … e della **fu** Donna Faustina Cimmino*», act 49 «*figlio del **fu** Filippo … e della **fu** Lucrezia Varrecchia*». Four dead parents marked on one sheet, and these two not. His baptism of 1 February 1792 makes him seventy-two.
«*e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***» — alive, unmarked, on the same evidence as her husband. Her latest previous sighting was her son Raffaele's marriage act of 7 March 1844.

A CHILD OF GENERATION THREE THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **STANISLAO FALCO**, di anni **VENTIQUATTRO**, nato in **ARIENZO**, di professione **PASTORE**, domiciliato in Arienzo, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato in Arienzo, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata ivi; e **FILOMENA DI LUCIA**, di anni ventitré, nata in Arienzo, figlia di fu [?] di Lucia, **muratore**, e di **MARTA di NIZZO***». Church celebration **23 September 1861**, parish of **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**. **A PASTORE — a shepherd — in a house of contadini.** Twenty-four in September 1861 gives **b. c.1837**, which would make Andreana Crisci about forty at his birth: late, but this register's ages are good to about three years and no better, and she was bearing children into 1828 on the archive's own reckoning.

ALIVE AT SIXTY-NINE, three years before the other sighting. «*figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **Arienzo***» — **no «fu», no «defunto»**, in an act that marks the bride's father dead in the very next clause («*figlia di **fu** [?] di Lucia*»).

«*e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***» — alive, unmarked, on the same evidence. This is the Andreana Crisci who married Vincenzo Falco in December 1814, not the other woman of the name this archive keeps separate.

Stanislao Falco's bride: **twenty-three**, born Arienzo, so b. c.1838. **Her parents are LUIGI DI LUCIA, *muratore*, and MARTA DI NIZZO** — the father's forename is illegible on the marriage act itself and comes from the **NOTIFICAZIONI register bound into the same volume**, which gives the same couple in a clerk's cleaner hand: «*matrimonio tra **STANISLAO FALCO** figlio di **VINCENZO** e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, e **FILOMENA DI LUCIA** figlia di **LUIGI** e di **MARTA DI NIZZO***». Her father was already dead at the wedding. Her father is a ***muratore*** — a mason, **a lettered-adjacent trade in this corpus**, where nearly every man is a contadino, colono or bracciale.

THE REGISTER ACT BEHIND THE INDEX ENTRY. Act 14: «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **ANDREA FALCO maggiore**, di anni **VENTIQUATTRO**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **strada Camellara**, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato ivi, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, di professione **FILATRICE**, domiciliata ivi; e **MARIA CARMELA BUONO maggiore**, di anni ventiquattro, di professione filatrice, nata in Arienzo, domiciliata in **strada Porta di Sopra***». Church **24 May 1846** at Sant'Andrea, which is the date the index gave. Witnesses Agostino di Giglio and **Gennaro Laudato**. **TWENTY-FOUR IN MAY 1846 GIVES b. c.1822** — four years before Angelandrea, and the two are separate men on the ages alone.

**«MINORE» — AND THAT ONE WORD CONFIRMS HIS BIRTH ACT.** Act on img4r: «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **ANGELANDREA FALCO MINORE**, di anni **venti[…]**, nato in Arienzo, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **strada Camellara**, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, **colono**, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, **filatrice** … e **MARIA CIMMINO maggiore** … nata in Arienzo, domiciliata in **strada Capodiconca**, figlia di **ALESSANDRO CIMMINO**, contadino*». Witnesses **Gennaro Laudato** and Francesco de Angelis. **MAJORITY WAS TWENTY-ONE**, so «minore» puts him under it — and his birth act of **12 September 1826** makes him twenty years and six months. Maria Cimmino» on **17 April 1847** from a parish ark — the same bride, three weeks later. Both are kept.

**HER TRADE, FOR THE FIRST TIME: FILATRICE — a spinner.** «*e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, di professione **filatrice**, domiciliata ivi*». Alive and unmarked, and given the same way again on 29 March 1847. This archive had her age five times and her occupation never.

Andrea Falco's bride: twenty-four, **filatrice**, born Arienzo, of **strada Porta di Sopra**, daughter of **ONOFRIO BUONO** and **ANGELA IMBIMBO** — the parents from the index, now with her own age, trade and street.

«e di Giuseppe Falco, di anni trentasei, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara» — declaring the death of a neighbour, Emanuela d'Onofrio, with Domenico Balletta, 40, sartore, of the same street. Same age, same trade, same street, four weeks apart — one man, not two. Balletta is his neighbour in October 1817 as well.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni quarantadue, di professione Contadino, regnicolo, domiciliato strada Camellara» — THE FIRST CIVIL RECORD TO STATE HIS PARENTAGE OUTRIGHT. The clerk adds «fu Matteo» to tell him from the other Giuseppe Falco of the town, and in doing so confirms from the civil series what the archive previously had only from the parish books: this Giuseppe is a son of the late Matteo Falco. Forty-two here, so born about 1781 — which agrees within a year with the thirty-seven he gives in October 1817. (This archive published «quarantatre» until 20 September 2026. The word ends «-adue», and the same clerk's «tre», three lines below on the same leaf, is a different shape.) He declares with Cesare Giglio, 50, of the same street, at the death of Maria Crisci, three years old, daughter of Marcello Crisci and Maria Rosa Mauro.

«sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni quarantadue, di professione Contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Sant'Andrea, vicino della defunta» — atto 39, the SECOND «fu Matteo» sighting in two days, at the death of Antonia Cossi, nine months old, daughter of Francesco Cossi and a MARIA FALCO. TWO CAUTIONS. He is forty-two here and forty-three the day before, from the same clerk — a plain measure of how loosely these ages are kept. And he is given here on STRADA SANT'ANDREA where the day before he is on strada Camellara: in this form a declarant described as «vicino» is recorded at the street of the house where the death happened, so a declarant's street is NOT reliable evidence of where he himself lived. RE-READ 16 Sep 2026: the second declarant, not recorded here before, is ANIELLO DIGLIO, 46, contadino, «domiciliato ivi strada Sant'Andrea, vicino della defunta». He stands with a Falco over this household's dead again in April 1825.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, ZIO DEL DEFUNTO» — CORRECTED 16 Sep 2026: this archive read «vicino del defunto». The word is ZIO, and it is written twice on this act, once for each brother. Declaring beside his brother PASQUALE FALCO: the only act found so far in which the two appear together, and the first to give Giuseppe's trade as colono rather than contadino. Forty-two here, so born about 1782. AND HE COULD NOT WRITE: the act closes by naming him as the declarant who «dichiarato di non sapere scrivere per non averlo mai imparato», while Pasquale signs. What the word «zio» does and does not establish about MARIA FALCO is set out on Pasquale's row for this same act; it is recorded and not resolved.

«sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione MASSARO, regnicolo, domiciliato in strada Camellara, vicino della defunta, ed ANIELLO DIGLIO, di anni quarantasei, contadino» — a seventh sighting, and THE THIRD TIME HE STANDS FOR THE SAME HOUSE. Francesco Cossi and Maria Falco lost Antonia in June 1823, Giuseppe in March 1824 and Giuseppa here in April 1825, and Giuseppe Falco declared every one. CORRECTED 16 Sep 2026: this archive wrote here that the register called him «vicino» each time and never stated a relationship. THE MIDDLE ACT OF THE THREE CALLS HIM «ZIO DEL DEFUNTO». So the register does state a relationship, and this reading — a pattern of appearances but no statement of kinship — was built on a misread word. What stands is that he is «vicino della defunta» on THIS act and on the 1823 act, and «zio» in 1824 and «parente» in 1828: the clerk wrote whichever the declarant offered, and a man could be both the neighbour and the uncle on one street. His trade drifts again: contadino in 1823, colono in 1824, MASSARO here; and his age goes backwards, forty here against forty-two the year before.

**Verified against the image, work-list row 58: act 17, and «di anni QUARANTA, di professione MASSARO» is exactly what it says.** The other declarant is **ANIELLO DIGLIO, forty-six**, contadino of the same street — **and eleven weeks later, in act 34 of this same volume, the same Aniello Diglio of strada Camellara is FIFTY**. **Four years in seventy-eight days**, beside this archive's own demonstration that Giuseppe Falco went from forty to forty-five in four. **The register does not know how old anybody is.**

«è morta nella sua propria casa MADDALENA FALCO, d'anni SETTE, nata in Arienzo, di professione Contadina, figlia di GIUSEPPE FALCO, di professione Contadino, e di ANTONIA DI GUIDA» — atto 30. THIS CLOSES A LIFE THE ARCHIVE HAD ONLY OPENED: her civil birth act of 7 June 1818 records her born on strada Camellara to Giuseppe, thirty-six, and Antonia, and she died a week short of her seventh birthday. A documented grandchild of Matteo Falco and Francesca Crisci, and a first cousin of Vincenzo Falco's children. THE GIVEN NAME DID NOT RESOLVE IN THE CIVIL HAND at the leaf's maximum resolution. It is supplied by the PARISH page, which was already harvested into this repository and never parsed: `3Q9M-CSD3-13CH-7`, an October 1819 baptism «et Josepho Falco et Anto[nia] di [Guida] Conjugibus», margin «Cresantios» = CRESCENTIUS. Two independent sources, same parents, same month. Graded PROBABLE on the civil act and PROVEN on the join.

Aged FORTY, contadino. He was given as THIRTY-SIX on 7 June 1818, sixteen months earlier — four years of ageing in sixteen months, from one clerk's desk. A fresh instance of the stated-age problem, in the household that supplies most of them.
«d'anni TRENTUNO» — thirty-one, so b. c.1788. This archive has already established that the civil clerks' age for her is about five years out; the figure is recorded, not believed.

THE CIVIL ACT BEHIND THE CHURCH DATE, AND IT DATES HIS BIRTH. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **CRESCENZO FALCO maggiore di anni VENTICINQUE nato in ARIENZO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato **IVI strada Sant'Andrea**, figlio di **GIUSEPPE FALCO** di professione simile domiciliato **ivi**, e di **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** di professione contadina domiciliata **ivi***» — TRANSCRIPTION CORRECTED 16 Sep 2026: this archive wrote «domiciliato **in** strada Sant'Andrea» and the act reads «domiciliato **ivi** strada Sant'Andrea». The dropped word matters, because «ivi» in these forms means THE COMUNE and not the street — the bride in this very act is «domiciliata **ivi strada Cappuccini**», one word and two streets. So GIUSEPPE FALCO and ANTONIA DI GUIDA are recorded here as domiciled AT ARIENZO, and THE ACT DOES NOT GIVE THEIR STREET. Anything this archive concluded about the household leaving strada Camellara rests on a word that was never there — bride **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO**, 23, contadina, of strada Cappuccini, «*figlia di **GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO** … e di **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE** … **defunta***». The INDICAZIONE records the church celebration: **3 February 1845**, parish of **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**, witnesses **Luigi Verdicchio** and **Nunzio Rivetti**. TWENTY-FIVE ON 2 FEBRUARY 1845 puts his birth between 3 February 1819 and 2 February 1820 — and his civil birth act is 11 October 1819.

**RE-READ IN FULL, 20 September 2026, work-list row 58 — and one thing in it was nearly "corrected" and is right.** The act says «**maggiore** di anni venticinque», and «maggiore di anni X» is elsewhere a statement of legal majority, not of age; on that reading the act would bound his birth on one side only and «it dates his birth» would be false. **The control is four lines below, in the same sentence: the bride is «maggiore di anni VENTITRE».** No age of majority is twenty-three. **So «maggiore» is a status and the number is the age**, for both of them, and the inference stands. Everything else verifies: act 3, «Domenico Zinelli Sindaco», Arienzo, **distretto di CASERTA**, ore ventuno; «domiciliato **ivi** strada Sant'Andrea»; the church celebration on **3 February** before **LUIGI VERDICCHIO** and **NUNZIO RIVETTI**.

Given with a trade and a domicile and NOT marked «defunto» — in an act that marks BOTH of the bride's parents dead in the same sentence. He was already known alive in November 1849 from his son the deacon's death act; this is an independent sighting on a form that states death explicitly rather than leaving it to be inferred.

HER LATEST DATED SIGHTING BY TWENTY-FIVE YEARS. This archive held her on one dated document — her son Crescenzo's birth act of 11 October 1819. Here she is «*di professione contadina domiciliata ivi*», alive, in an act that writes «DEFUNTO» and «DEFUNTA» for the bride's father and mother. HER DEATH HAS BEEN HUNTED THROUGH THE PARISH REGISTER AND NOT FOUND; the window now opens on 2 February 1845 instead of October 1819.

Crescenzo Falco's bride: twenty-three, contadina, born in Arienzo, and an orphan — «*figlia di GENNARO MORGILLO defunto, di professione colono … e di MARIA FELICIA SANSONE, di professione contadina … defunta*». The church act carries a dispensation «*super quarto gradu consanguinitatis*», so she and Crescenzo were third cousins.

**THE BAPTISM, FOUND — AND IT WAS NEVER ON THE LEAF THIS ARCHIVE KEPT RENDERING.** «*[Anno] D[omi]ni **1818**, die vero **septima 7 Junii**, R[everendu]s D[ominu]s **D. HYACINTHUS Archip[resbyter] MORGILLO*».

**Same day as her civil birth act**, which this archive already held. **The godmother is the same Dorotea d'Addio who stood at Gioacchino Falco's font in 1779** — forty years of one woman at this family's baptisms.

FROM THE MARGIN OF HIS OWN BIRTH ACT, not from any marriage register: «*Con atto **6 agosto 1856** at[to] **21** in **S[?] …a Vico** il Falco sposò **DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI** [di] **Gaspare**(?)*». **THE COMUNE IS NOT ESTABLISHED.** At five times magnification the place reads «*S[?]basia a Vico*» and resolves no further. **SANTA MARIA A VICO IS THE OBVIOUS CANDIDATE AND IS EXCLUDED BY ITS OWN REGISTER**: `an_ua55736`, *Matrimoni* 1856, **act 21 is Don Domenico de Lucia, 29, of San Felice, promised 14 June 1856** — no Falco, and no act of 6 August (act 31 is 3 August, act 32 is 9 August). **What is certain is the annotation itself**: a Falco of this house married a DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI on 6 August 1856, recorded as act 21 somewhere «…a Vico». **IT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS ARCHIVE USED A BIRTH-ACT MARGIN AS A SOURCE**, and the rule it produced — that a civil birth act can carry the child's later marriage, in another comune, where no local register shows it — has since found Pasqua Falco's marriage of 1880, Giovanna Arricale's of 1872 and **both** of Domenica Falco's, of 1874 and 1881.

His parents, from the 1816 register: SIMONE MORGILLO and GAETANA LAUDATO, who died on 9 March 1816 aged seventy-eight, «vedova di Simone Morgillo», of strada Trave. Angelo declared it himself, aged fifty-eight — which is exactly seventy in 1828.

«*a' detto dì **nove** del mese corrente di **APRILE** ad ore dodici … **GAETANA LAUDATO** figlia delli furono **GIACINTO LAUDATO** e **VITTORIA RUOTOLO**, **VEDOVA DI SIMONE MORGILLO**, di anni **SETTANTOTTO**, contadina, domiciliata nella strada Trave*» — declared by her own sons **ANGELO MORGILLO**, 48, and **GIUSEPPE MORGILLO**, 71, «*figli della defunta*». **TWO CORRECTIONS, 20 Sep 2026, both from the image: the date was published as 9 MARCH and the act says 9 APRIL; and the mother was published as «Giovanna —», her surname unread, when the act plainly reads VITTORIA RUOTOLO.** — born about 1738, the deepest this archive reaches into the Morgillo.

«GENNARO MORGILLO, vedovo di Felicia Sompone, nato in Arienzo, di anni cinquantatré, di professione COLONO, domiciliato STRADA CAMELLARA, figlio di ANGELO MORGILLO defunto, di professione COLONO» — born about 1790. A THIRD SON of the colono Angelo, and the one who left the hill: he lived on strada Camellara, the Falco street. HIS DEATH WAS DECLARED BY GIUSEPPE FALCO, colono of the same street. (Dated 14 August here until 20 September 2026; the act reads «il dì quattro del mese di Agosto», and the acts either side of it are 3 August and 10 August.)

**THIS ARCHIVE SAID, UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, THAT THE ACT WAS «THE CLOSEST THE RECORD COMES TO THE FALCO-MORGILLO MARRIAGE THAT WAS STILL THIRTY YEARS AWAY». THAT WAS WRONG BY TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS, AND THE ARCHIVE'S OWN FILES SAID SO.** Eighteen months after this act, on **2 February 1845**, **CRESCENZO FALCO** — Giuseppe's son, of this same strada Camellara — married **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO**, twenty-three, of **strada Cappuccini**, «*figlia di GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO, di professione colono, e di MARIA FELICIA SANSONE … defunta*».

**PROBABLE, NOT PROVEN: the Gennaro Morgillo who died here is very likely her father.** Four things agree — the forename and surname; the trade, *colono*, in both acts; the wife, a **Felicia** already dead when he died a widower in 1843 and «defunta» in 1845; and the street, since the bride lived on **strada Cappuccini** and this Gennaro's father Angelo was the colono of the **Monticello de' Cappuccini**, the hill that street climbs. **And the wife's surname, which could not be read on 20 September, was read the same day.** The word in the 1843 act is **«Sanſone»** — SANSONE — with the long ſ that this archive published as a «p» when it wrote «Sompone». The control is in the next volume it checked: Arienzo Morti 1826 act 22 is declared by **ANGELO SANSONE** of this same strada Camellara, and the two words are the same shape, letter for letter. **So the 1845 act's MARIA FELICIA SANSONE and the 1843 act's FELICIA SANSONE are one name**, s and z being interchangeable in these registers.

**Five things now agree, and one of them is a whole second name.** What is still missing is a document that says so. Morgillo is the commonest surname on these pages and this archive already holds two distinct Angelo Morgillo. **What would settle it is the marriage's own dossier**: the *processetto* for Arienzo 1845 must contain Gennaro Morgillo's death certificate, and that certificate will carry an act number. If it is 33 of 1843, this is him.

**The 1840 act gives him no age at all** — he is named in it as the dead child's father, and fathers are not aged in these acts. **The 1843 act says forty-three, not forty-eight**; this archive read that from the image on 15 September 2026 and corrected it in one file only. **So the series is forty-seven in August 1842 and forty-three in September 1843. **The two men who declared her death were also mis-aged**: **CLEMENTE CIOFFI is thirty-six**, not thirty-four, and **VIRGILIO CIOFFI is twenty-three**, not twenty-eight. Both of strada Camellara — a fourth and fifth Cioffi on the Falco street.

Named in two death acts two years apart, with the same rank and trade both times: as father of **MARIA GIUSEPPA SCARPATI** (Morti 1840 atto 28) and as father of **DON ANGELO SCARPATI, ARCIPRETE OF ARIENZO** (Morti 1842 atto 15). **Both acts also agree on the mother's name**, once the 1840 act is read properly — see Donna Faustina Cimmino below.

The 1840 act names the mother SERAFINA Cimmino; the 1842 act names her FAUSTINA Cimmino… Either a clerk misread a forename, or Stefano Scarpati married twice.*» **Both acts say FAUSTINA.** There was no second wife to wonder about and no clerk to blame: **the misreading was this archive's**, and a woman called Donna Serafina Cimmino, who never existed, had a name on this site.

**What it costs and what it buys.** It removes an invented person and an invented problem, and it **strengthens the join**: the archpriest of Arienzo and the sorora of the Conservatorio di San Filippo are now named in two acts two years apart with **the same father, the same rank, the same trade and the same mother**. **THE MARRIAGE, FOUND** — this archive held the household from its children alone. **RE-READ IN FULL FROM THE IMAGE, 20 September 2026, work-list row 58**, and the reading below replaces one that put a «fu» in front of four names the act never puts one in front of.

«*L'anno mille ottocento **sessanta**, il dì **VENTUNO** di **Gennajo**, alle ore ventitre, avanti di Noi **Stefano Sargenti**, uffiziale dello Stato Civile di **ARIENZO**, distretto di **CASERTA** … sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **SABBATINO ANNECCHINO**, di anni **trentaquattro**, nato in **FORCHIA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **Forchia**, figlio di **CARMINE ANNECCHINO defunto** … e di **ROSA CEGLIA defunta** … e **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA**, di anni **ventinove**, nata in **ARIENZO**, domiciliata in Arienzo, figlia di **VALERIO CARFORA**, di professione contadino, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **PASQUA MORGILLO defunta***».

**THREE THINGS CHANGE.** The act is of **21 January**, not the twentieth — «*il dì **ventuno***». The groom's own spelling is **SABBATINO**, with two b. And **the bride's father is not marked dead**: see Valerio Carfora below.

The church celebration followed on **22 January**, before witnesses read here as **PASQUALE LAUDATO** and **ANTONIO CRISCI** — the last surname is **Crisci**, with no descender, and was published as «Crispi». **How the three lines divide into two witnesses is not certain**: the clerk writes «*Pasquale Lau=/dato, di Antonio/ Crisci*» with no conjunction, and it may be one man «Pasquale Laudato di Antonio» and a second surnamed Crisci. **Left as it reads.**

SABATINO'S FATHER, AND A GENERATION THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE. «*figlio di **fu CARMINE ANNECCHINO**, di professione **contadino***» — dead before January 1860, of Forchia. **NOT the Carmine Annecchino who married Maria Carfora and fathered Filomena in 1897**; that one was bearing children from 1883 and is two generations later. **The name recurs in this family**, which is worth holding onto rather than resolving.
«*e di **ROSA CEGLIA defunta***» — Sabatino Annecchino's mother, dead before January 1860. **CEGLIA HAS NEVER APPEARED IN THIS ARCHIVE**, under any spelling.

«*MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA, di anni **ventinove**, **nata in ARIENZO***» — so born about 1831, and **an Arienzo woman, not a Forchia one**. This archive had her only as a mother of four daughters born 1861–1866.

**MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA'S FATHER — AND HE WAS ALIVE, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE HAD SAID HE WAS NOT.** «*figlia di **VALERIO CARFORA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi***» — and **there the sentence stops**. The act writes «**defunto**» after Carmine Annecchino, «**defunta**» after Rosa Ceglia and «**defunta**» after Pasqua Morgillo. **It writes nothing after him.**

**And the act proves it a second time, in its own list of documents.** Item **6** of the eight papers read into the marriage is «*Nel **CONSENSO DEL PADRE** della stessa, **dato nell'atto***» — the bride's father consented **in person, in the act**, on 21 January 1860. **A dead man does not consent.**

**THE FORENAME RESOLVES, AND IT WAS NEVER ILLEGIBLE — IT WAS SPLIT.** This archive recorded «*the word reads «[L/t]erio» at four times magnification and is left unread rather than guessed*». **The word is not one word.** It wraps across the column: the line ends «*figlia di **Va***» and the next begins «***lerio** Carfora*». **VALERIO** — and no other Italian forename ends in *-lerio*. **The archive magnified the second half of a word and called the whole of it illegible.**

**So the Carfora are an Arienzo family as well as a Forchia one**, and **Valerio Carfora, contadino of Arienzo, was living there in January 1860** — a man to look for, not a death to look for.

«*e di **PASQUA MORGILLO defunta***» — Maria Antonia Carfora's mother, **dead before 21 January 1860**, and the only one of the bride's two parents the act does mark. **A CARFORA–MORGILLO marriage at Arienzo**, in the generation born about 1800.

**Her death act is in the marriage's own dossier**: item **7** of the eight documents read into the act is «*Nell'atto di morte della madre della stessa*». **The Arienzo processetto for 1860 would hand over the date, the street and her parents in one page.**

GENERATION FIVE. Son of Raffaele Falco and Angela Rosa Morgillo. MARRIED GIOVANNA ARRICALE ON 18 NOVEMBER 1872 AT ARIENZO — the date, not just the year. Named in his son's marriage dossier of 1897 and again in his daughter's banns of 1902 — «figlia di CARMINANTONIO, residente in Arienzo». THE TWO DOCUMENTS DISAGREE ABOUT HIS AGE: forty-six in August 1897, fifty-five in August 1902 — nine years of ageing in five years. The archive publishes the discrepancy rather than smoothing it

Named in both documents as the mother — «e figlia di ARRICALE GIOVANNA, contadina». HER PARENTS ARE READ FROM THE IMAGE: FRANCESCO ARRICALE, 24, contadino, and PASQUA FALCO, 25, both of STRADA CAPODICONCA, in her own birth act — atto 114 of 1848, born 22 December 1848. Confirmed independently by the indexed marriage record of 18 Nov 1872 in the Caserta SMCV Tribunale collection (1:2:HHBF-FZWK, image 3QS7-L976-QW8C). HER MOTHER WAS A FALCO — so generation five's groom and his bride's mother shared a surname. NO KINSHIP IS CLAIMED: Arienzo holds several Pasqua Falco in these years, mothers of Maione, Majone and Loffredo children among others, and this one is not identified beyond the act. HER SIBLINGS ARE NOT FINDABLE and the index is the reason: the Caserta collection covering 1809-1866 holds 1,086 Falco records for Arienzo and effectively NO Arricale at all, so it cannot show children of this couple. Use the full-text page transcripts for Arricale, not the name index The Arricale of Arienzo are a large and steady family of VATICALI — carriers — chiefly of strada Capodiconca, and the spelling wanders between Arricale, Arrigale and Arricole in the same decade and sometimes the same hand

That is eighteen months before this marriage, it agrees on the trade, on the wife's forename and on her being dead first, and the bride's **strada Cappuccini** is the hill where that Angelo Morgillo's house stood. **It is graded PROBABLE and no more**, because Morgillo is the commonest surname in these registers. **AND THE WIFE'S SURNAME NOW AGREES TOO.** The 1843 word was published as «Sompone» and read on 20 September as **«Sanſone»** — SANSONE — against a control on the same street: Arienzo Morti 1826 act 22, declared by **ANGELO SANSONE** of strada Camellara, whose surname is written in the same hand-shape, long ſ and all. **What this archive had taken for a «p» is a long s.** So the mother named here is the woman named there. **The 1845 processetto would settle it in one line**, by quoting the death act's number.

«*e di **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE**, di professione **contadina** … **defunta***» — from her daughter's marriage act of 2 February 1845.

**PUBLISHED HERE AS «SANSONE» UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND WITH IT THE CLAIM THAT THE SURNAME «HAD NEVER APPEARED IN THIS ARCHIVE AT ALL».** The letter is a long **ſ**, not a **z**, and the test is on the same leaf: **«Crescenzo», in the groom's own name, has a z** — a compact loop that drops below the line and has no ascender. **The letter in this surname rises above the x-height before it descends.** A z in this hand does not do that.

**So the surname was not new.** **ANGELO SANSONE**, contadino of **strada Camellara**, declares the death of Maria Falco, wife of Alfonso Diglio, on 25 April 1826 — and his surname is written in the same shape. **Three acts now agree: 1826, 1843 and 1845, all SANSONE.** Not claimed as kin.

Twenty-three, contadina, born in Arienzo, and an orphan of both parents when she married **CRESCENZO FALCO**. The church act carries a dispensation «*super quarto gradu consanguinitatis*», so she and her husband were third cousins — the fourth Falco marriage inside the fourth degree this archive holds.

THE CONTROL THAT SEPARATES THE TWO SURNAMES. «*è comparso **FRANCESCO COSSI**, di anni **trenta**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in detto comune, **strada COSSI***» — the same word twice in one sentence, as a name and as a street, which checks the reading with no judgement at all. Thirty in 1819, so b. c.1789. **The strada Camellara FRANCESCO CIOFFI is twenty-seven in 1824, b. c.1797. Different men, different ages, different streets.** Not kin to the Falco; recorded to hold the two families apart.

«*e da **TERESA MORGILLO** sua moglie legitima d'anni **ventotto***» — twenty-eight, so b. c.1791. She is the wife of the strada Cossi Francesco, NOT of the strada Camellara Francesco Cioffi, whose wife is **MARIA FALCO**.

THE ACT THAT JOINS TWO HOUSEHOLDS THIS ARCHIVE KEPT APART. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **MICHELE FALCO maggiore, di anni QUARANTATRE, nato in ARIENZO, di professione COLONO, domiciliato in STRADA CAMELLARA, figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO DEFUNTO**, di professione simile, domiciliato ivi, e di **CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA**, di professione filatrice … **VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI** … e **GIOVANNA D'AMBROGIO maggiore, di anni DICIANNOVE**, di professione contadina*». **«Michele Falco & Antonia Vigliotta» and «Michele Falco & Maria Giovanna d'Ambrogio» are ONE MAN AND TWO MARRIAGES.** The d'Ambrogio household was known only by a daughter **Antonia born 19 November 1850** — nine months after this wedding.

**Verified against the image, work-list row 58 — act 6, and every word holds.** «*L'anno mille ottocento **cinquanta**, il dì **dodici** del mese di **Febrajo**, alle ore **sedici**, avanti di Noi **ARCANGELO DE FUSCO Sindaco***». **The bride's parents had never been recorded here**: **DOMENICO D'AMBROGIO defunto**, contadino, and **CARMINA MANNA**, **filatrice**, and she is of **strada Sant'Andrea**. The church celebration followed the same day at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**, before **ALFONSO VERDICCHIO** and a **CLEMENTE MOR[GILLO]**.

«*VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI*» — she was dead by 12 February 1850. Her daughter Chiara died in 1846 aged seven and her daughter Carmela on 4 August 1859, which is AFTER this date and therefore a child of the first marriage buried nine years into the second.

MICHELE FALCO'S FATHER, NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME: «*figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO DEFUNTO**, di professione **simile** [colono], domiciliato **ivi** [strada Camellara]*». A generation this archive did not have for this house. NOT joined to the direct line's Raffaele Falco of 1818, who was thirty-one and alive in 1850.

«*e di **CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA**, di professione **filatrice***». **A NAME THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HAS, AND THIS IS ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT HER.** Generation two's wife CHIARA RIVETTI was the widow of **PASQUALE** Falco, died 13 September 1843 aged eighty, and bore Pasquale children from 1789 to 1802 — so she cannot have been married to a Raffaele Falco when this Michele was born about 1807. **Either a second Chiara Rivetti, on a street where the Rivetti are dense, or Michele's stated age is badly wrong. Nothing is merged and nothing is chosen.**

«figlio di MICHELE FALCO, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi» — from the death act of his two-year-old son Matteo Falco, Arienzo Morti 1842 atto 55, 25 August 1842, read at 2800px. Named WITHOUT «fu», so alive. A contadino on strada Camellara, the street of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti. NO ACT NAMES HIS PARENTS. He is not placed in the line here, and the archive will not place him until an act does.

«e di ANTONIA MIGLIORE, domiciliata ivi» — same act, also without «fu», so alive in 1842. Migliore is a common Arienzo surname and no parents are named for her.

**HER SURNAME WAS PUBLISHED HERE AS «MIGLIORE» UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026.** The act reads «*e di **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, domiciliata ivi*», and the word was set beside the same clerk's «Antonia Vigliotta» in the death act of **MARIA ROSA FALCO**, 30 May 1834, and found to be the same word — the same capital **V**, the same «gli» with its tall l, the same «-otta». **Migliore has no V and no double t.**

**And the marriage act settles it from the other end**: on 12 February 1850 **MICHELE FALCO, colono of strada Camellara**, marries again as «***VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI***». **One wife, one surname, three acts — 1834, 1842 and 1850.**

«è morto nella sua propria casa MATTEO FALCO D'ANNI DUE, nato in Arienzo» — died at ten at night on 24 August 1842, aged two, so born about 1840. HIS NAME IS THE QUESTION. Neapolitan custom named a first son for his father's father, and the name at the head of this line is MATTEO FALCO, who married Francesca Crisci. That is a reason to look for Michele among Matteo's sons. IT IS NOT EVIDENCE. A naming habit is not a record, and this archive does not build a generation out of one.

**His mother is ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA, not «Antonia Migliore»** — corrected 20 September 2026 from the image, against the same clerk's spelling in the 1834 act and against his father's own remarriage of 1850 as «vedovo di ANTONIA VIGLIOTI».

**Forty-seven**, a contadino of strada Camellara — verified from the image, «*di anni quarantasette*». He is a neighbour; the act does not call him kin, and these registers write «parente» when they mean it.

**THE CLAIM THAT USED TO STAND HERE WAS THE OPPOSITE OF THE TRUTH.** This page said: «*Thirteen months later, at forty-eight, the same man reports the death of CHIARA RIVETTI on the same street. In a register that gives Giuseppe Falco four different ages, this one holds.*» **He is not forty-eight in that act. He is forty-three.** The archive read «quarantatre» from the image on 15 September 2026 and corrected Chiara Rivetti's act — and left the boast standing in two other files. **Forty-seven in August 1842, forty-three in September 1843: he lost four years in thirteen months, and this is one more demonstration that the ages in these registers are guessed.**

Thirty-two, a contadino of strada Camellara. **HIS SURNAME WAS PUBLISHED HERE AS «CIOFFI» UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 AND IT IS NOT CIOFFI.** The control is two lines below it in the same act: **GIOVANNI CIOFFI**, written with the unmistakable double-f ligature and its long descender. **This word has no such ligature.** It reads **«Gasparo»** — a capital with a descending loop, «a», a long ſ, then «aro».

**Gasparo is an Arienzo surname**, not a guess: the 1834 death register has **Elena Lettieri, «widow of ANGELO GASPARO»**, and the same volume records a **strada Gasparro**. **The reading is probable and is not settled** — at 1,622 pixels across a half page, which is where this filming stops, the capital will not separate from a C. **What is settled is the negative: he is not one of the Cioffi of this street.**

«*è morto nella sua propria casa **SALVATORE FALCO, di mesi QUATTORDICI**, nato in Arienzo, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, figlio di **MICHELE FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, domiciliata ivi*» — **image 30 RIGHT**, 9 August 1836. Fourteen months, so born about June 1835.

**HIS MOTHER IS NAMED, AND SHE IS THE REASON THIS HOUSEHOLD IS NO LONGER «UNJOINED».** **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA** is the wife of the **MICHELE FALCO of strada Camellara** whose other children this archive holds — Maria Rosa in 1834, Matteo in 1842 — and who married again in 1850 as «*vedovo di **ANTONIA VIGLIOTI***». **The clerks write her Antonia and Mariantonia indifferently; it is one woman in four acts.**

**THIS ROW STOOD IN A HOUSEHOLD OF ITS OWN, «Michele Falco (unjoined)», UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026.** Reading the act gave the mother's name, and the mother's name joined it to a household this archive already had. **The stub was not a family. It was a line nobody had read.**

«*è morta nella sua propria casa **MARIA ROSA FALCO, di mesi VENTIDUE**, nata in Arienzo, di professione contadina, domiciliata ivi, figlia di **MICHELE FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, domiciliata ivi*» — **IMAGE 24 RIGHT**, 30 May 1834.

**SHE WAS PUBLISHED HERE AT «d'anni SEDICI» — SIXTEEN YEARS — AND SHE WAS TWENTY-TWO MONTHS.** The act reads «*di **mesi** ventidue*», magnified. **A sixteen-year-old contadina and an infant of not quite two are not the same kind of person**: everything anyone might infer from the first — a birth about 1818, a working girl, a daughter of marriageable age — is wrong. She was born about **July 1832**.

**Her mother was not recorded either.** **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA** is named in the act. **And she raises a question this archive should not settle by guessing**: the Michele Falco of Arienzo who buries a two-year-old son in 1842 is married to an **ANTONIA MIGLIORE**. Same forename, same town, same trade, eight years apart. **Either one of the two surnames is misread, or there are two Michele Falco each married to an Antonia.** Neither is asserted.

**The citation also pointed at image 23 right**, which is Carmina Zimbardo, fourteen days old, daughter of Domenico Zimbardo and Orsola Porrino.

**THIS ROW STOOD IN A HOUSEHOLD OF ITS OWN, «Michele Falco (strada Camellara)», UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026.** The act names her mother — **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA** — and that name joins her to a household this archive already had: the **MICHELE FALCO of strada Camellara** who buried Salvatore in 1836 and Matteo in 1842 and married again in 1850 as «*vedovo di ANTONIA VIGLIOTI*». **The stub was not a family. It was a line nobody had read.**

«*è comparso **ANIELLO CARFORA**, di anni **trentuno**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in questo Comune **STRADA CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato un **Maschio***» — atto of 10 January 1831. **A CARFORA HOUSEHOLD ON THE FALCO'S OWN STREET**, thirty years before the marriage act that first told this archive the Carfora were an Arienzo family at all. Thirty-one here, so born about 1800 — the same generation as «[?]erio Carfora», Maria Antonia's father. **He is not that man**: this one's wife is Orsola Porrino. THIS HOUSEHOLD IS NOT JOINED TO ANY OTHER IN THIS ARCHIVE. It is recorded because work-list row 63 asked whether the Carfora were an Arienzo family at all, and the answer is that they were — three separate Carfora households appear in a single year of one register. Whether any of them is the house of «[?]erio Carfora and Pasqua Morgillo» is NOT established and is not claimed.

**Verified against the image, work-list row 58 — and the act has a number this archive never recorded: it is ATTO 6.** The parish named in the second column is **SANT'ANDREA APOSTOLO DI ARIENZO**. The witness to the presentation is **MARCELLO RIVETTI, forty-eight**, contadino — a Rivetti of the right generation on the Falco's street, recorded and not claimed.
